American Robin: cheerily, cheer-up, cheerio — a caroling whistle
Northern Cardinal: birdie, birdie, birdie, or cheer, cheer, cheer
Black-capped Chickadee: says its name, chick-a-dee-dee-dee; song is a sweet two-note hey, sweetie
Carolina Wren: teakettle, teakettle, teakettle — very loud for a tiny bird
House Wren: a bubbly, tumbling song that sounds like a pot boiling over
Song Sparrow: maids, maids, maids, put on your teakettle-ettle-ettle
House Finch: a long, cheerful, rambling warble that often ends in a buzzy zeee
Mourning Dove: a soft, sad who-OOO-oo-oo-oo, often mistaken for an owl
Blue Jay: a loud jay, jay; also a squeaky note like an old water pump
European Starling: a copycat full of wolf whistles, clicks, and squeaks
Gray Catbird: a call like a cat's meow; song is a jumbled, scratchy medley
Brown Thrasher: says every phrase twice — plant-a-seed, plant-a-seed, bury-it, bury-it, pull-it-up, pull-it-up
Baltimore Oriole: a rich whistle — here, here, come right here, dear
Chipping Sparrow: a dry, flat trill, like a sewing machine
Downy Woodpecker: a sharp pik; also a whinny that falls in pitch, like a tiny horse
Northern Flicker: a long, laughing wick-wick-wick-wick; also a loud kyeer
White-breasted Nuthatch: a nasal yank, yank, like a tiny toy horn
Red-eyed Vireo: here I am, where are you, over here, see me — repeated all day long
Warbling Vireo: if I sees you, I will seize you, and I'll squeeze you till you squirt
Eastern Phoebe: says its name in a raspy fee-bee
Rose-breasted Grosbeak: sounds like a robin that took opera lessons
Scarlet Tanager: sounds like a robin with a sore throat
Indigo Bunting: notes in pairs — fire! fire! where? where? here! here! put it out!
Belted Kingfisher: a loud, dry rattle, like a fishing reel
Common Grackle: a squeak like a rusty gate
Bobolink: a bubbly, robot-like jumble, like R2-D2 from Star Wars
Field Sparrow: speeds up like a ping-pong ball bouncing to a stop
Yellow Warbler: sweet, sweet, sweet, I'm so sweet!
Sandhill Crane: a rolling, rattling bugle that sounds prehistoric
Barred Owl: who cooks for you? who cooks for you-all?
Red-tailed Hawk: a raspy, drawn-out scream — the eagle sound used in movies
Dark-eyed Junco: a musical trill and a sharp smack call
